title: Parallel independent voltage computing along dendrites of CA3 pyramidal neurons.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Dryad deposit doi:10.5061/dryad.hmgqnkb07 (CC0, v3, 2026-07-13, 6 files, 104.5 GB total). Scripted downloads are blocked (403 / proof-of-work bot wall); I solved the challenge and pulled README.md (3.2 kB) and preprocessing.zip (4.75 MB), then used HTTP range requests to extract 9 of the 11 real members of analysis.zip (144.8 MB) without downloading it whole. Loaded all 6 small pandas pickles (needed pandas 3.0; local pandas 2.3.3 cannot unpickle them). Main table df_fig1H_L.pkl = 2,748 rows x 28 columns, 134 dendritic regions of interest (ROIs), 19 cells, 11 mice, but only 398 unique (cell, lap) pairs and the somatic label dur_soma is constant inside every one of those 398 groups, so there are 398 distinct label values, not 2,748. I re-ran the authors' own RandomForestRegressor from the notebook: their random 90/10 split gives test R-squared (fraction of variance explained) 0.40 while train is 0.91; 5-fold cross-validation holding out whole cells gives R-squared -0.14 (worse than predicting the mean) and holding out whole dendrites gives 0.19. Other tables: df_fig4_rew 248 rows, df_fig4_glb and df_w_glb 142 rows, df_fig4D 78 rows, df_fig4H 4 rows.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The abstract only (Science paper is paywalled, no PubMed Central copy, Europe PMC reports no full text and no supplementary files). I could not verify df_fig2H_I.pkl (155 MB uncompressed / 143 MB compressed, over the 50 MB download cap): I parsed its first 8.6 MB and confirmed it is a pickle holding a 'driver' DataFrame indexed by ROI names with repeated 979-value float64 blocks, but its row count is unverified. Two files the notebooks load are absent from the deposit (rf_sub2sub.joblib, the trained forest, and summary_model_fig2.pkl, the Keras network summary). No data dictionary exists for any column; the README documents only the raw-imaging preprocessing pipeline.

a1_downloadable.note: Public Dryad deposit under CC0, no login and no access application; but every scripted request is refused (403) or met with a proof-of-work bot wall, so a browser or a solved challenge is needed. I downloaded and opened the files.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The somatic-activity label is literally a column (dur_soma and its z-scored twin dur_soma_z) in df_fig1H_L.pkl, alongside the six features the authors used. Verified in the file.

a3_inputs_present.note: All six inputs sit in the same table: dendritic activity in five 24-cm track bins from -180 to -60 cm before the place field, plus path distance from the soma. No lookups needed. Verified in the file.

a4_units_stated.note: Weak pass: units are implied, never stated. Path distance is micrometres (only known from a notebook plot axis), activity is a normalised area-under-the-curve in arbitrary units, and the modelled label is its z-score. Internally consistent, but no documentation.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAILS. 2,748 rows are (dendrite x lap) pairs, but the somatic label is identical for all sibling dendrites of a cell on a lap: 398 unique (cell, lap) label values, from 19 cells in 11 mice. So the real labelled sample is 398 continuous observations, far under the ~1,500 needed for regression, and the next-largest tables are 248, 142, 78 and 4 rows. Counted directly in the file.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 0.16 GB processed tables; 104 GB if you want the raw imaging
a6_fits_laptop.note: The processed tables are trivial on a laptop. The raw route is not: three session archives of 53.4, 31.5 and 19.4 GB, and the README says the denoising step needs a CUDA-capable GPU.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Nothing to contradict: no full text available to compare against, and the Dryad file list, file sizes and loaded row counts all agreed with each other.

a8_label_provenance.note: The label is a real physical measurement (somatic membrane-voltage events from voltage imaging), not another model's output. Caveat: features and label come from the same imaging and event-detection pipeline, and the label repeats across sibling dendrites, which is what makes a random split leak.

existing_models.name: The paper's own RandomForestRegressor (scikit-learn, 2000 trees, depth 30) predicting z-scored somatic activity from five preceding dendritic track bins plus distance from soma, in Noguchi_etal_2026_Fig_1_H_L.ipynb
existing_models.score_and_split: Random 90/10 split of rows, random_state=42. Re-running it myself: test R-squared 0.40 vs train 0.91; holding out whole cells drops it to -0.14, holding out whole dendrites to 0.19. The saved model file rf_sub2sub.joblib is referenced by the notebook but is not in the deposit.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Not retrievable: the Science full text is paywalled, so I could not read their discussion.

existing_models.name: The paper's own Keras/TensorFlow dense network for Figure 2 (dendritic event 'driver' / 'follower' / 'sync' analysis), referenced in Noguchi_etal_2026_Fig_2.ipynb
existing_models.score_and_split: Unknown. The notebook only plots mean squared error from summary_model_fig2.pkl, which is not included in the deposit, and the architecture is not shown beyond Sequential/Dense imports.

backbone.name: None applicable
backbone.hardware: CPU laptop would suffice for the tables, but there is no pretrained backbone for six hand-engineered dendritic activity features; voltage-trace foundation models are not an option on 19 cells.

integration.partner_dataset: No clean partner. The only joinable keys are internal mouse/cell/ROI strings (stan95_1_basal1); there is no gene, protein, compound or genomic coordinate to join on.
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Cannot be written: nothing external joins to these internal ROI identifiers, so any combination would require re-processing raw imaging from another lab.

controls.positive_control: Available in principle: distance from soma must come out as the strongest single predictor of dendrite-soma coupling, a textbook result that the data reproduces (correlation of path distance with the somatic label -0.35).
controls.negative_control: Label shuffling is easy and in fact already instructive: the gap between the random-split R-squared of 0.40 and the leave-cells-out R-squared of -0.14 is itself a leakage demonstration.
controls.external_validation: None in the deposit. Related 2026 datasets exist (a Neuron paper on movement-stabilised CA1 dendritic recordings, a Science Advances paper on CA3 dendritic calcium spikes) but neither is a joinable table.

honest_claim_h3: At best: 'in 19 CA3 pyramidal cells from 11 mice recorded by one lab, the recent activity of a dendrite and its distance from the soma explain about a fifth of the lap-to-lap variance in that cell's somatic output when unseen dendrites are held out, and none of it when unseen cells are held out.'

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the recent activity of individual dendrites to predict how strongly their parent neuron's cell body fires on each lap.
plain_idea.train_on: One table of 2,748 rows, each a dendritic branch on one lap of a virtual-reality corridor, with its activity in five 24-cm bins of track before the place field and its path distance from the cell body; 134 branches, 19 cells, 11 mice.
plain_idea.predict: The parent cell body's voltage-event activity during the place field on that lap, measured by fast voltage imaging of a genetically encoded voltage sensor in the same recording.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Dendritic neuroscientists argue about whether branch activity predicts somatic output; a grouped-split re-analysis would show how much of the published prediction survives when whole cells are held out. Here it is answered in an afternoon and rests on only 398 independent measurements.

more_or_better_data.why: This is the only data for the task, and it is tiny: 398 independent somatic observations from 19 cells. The paper's own forest was trained on exactly these rows, so we would have no data advantage over it at all.

confidence_score.why: Laps repeat within a cell (9 to 45 per cell), so lap-to-lap spread gives a rough noise estimate, but with 19 cells any per-cell confidence estimate would itself be unstable, and no replicate recordings of the same cell exist.

models_beatable.why: A 2026 random forest evaluated on a random 90/10 split that puts the same somatic label value in train and test; I reproduced its 0.40 R-squared and showed it falls to -0.14 under leave-cells-out. Beating it honestly is easy; the problem is that nothing honest works well.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No accessible new data joins to this deposit: other dendritic recordings come from different labs, sensors and brain regions, and there is no shared identifier, so the 'same quantity, same assay, same split' condition fails outright.

label_elsewhere.sources: None. Somatic voltage-event activity per lap for an identified CA3 dendrite exists only in this recording; no public resource (searched for dendritic voltage imaging datasets and found only other labs' separate papers, not joinable tables) holds this label for other items.
label_elsewhere.why: With no external labelled set there is neither extra training data nor any way to test whether a model generalises beyond these 19 cells.

ml_idea: Re-evaluate the paper's own random forest (dendritic activity in five preceding track bins + path distance from soma -> z-scored somatic activity) under leave-one-cell-out and leave-one-dendrite-out cross-validation instead of the published random split. I already ran it: 0.40 becomes -0.14 (cells held out) and 0.19 (dendrites held out). The finding is real but it is a one-afternoon comment, not a project, and the 398 independent label values cannot support anything larger.

effort.compute_note: Measured, not guessed: I downloaded the tables, loaded them and ran both the authors' random-split fit and two grouped 5-fold cross-validations with 300-tree forests in under two minutes on this laptop; the 2 hours covers the bot-wall workaround and the pandas 3.0 environment needed to unpickle the files.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count unique values of the somatic label per (cell, lap): 398 unique values across 2,748 rows, 19 cells. That one count kills it, and it takes thirty seconds.

verdict_reason: Fails A5. The 2,748-row table looks adequate but the somatic label is duplicated across every sibling dendrite of a cell on a lap, leaving 398 independent continuous observations from 19 cells in 11 mice; every other table is 4 to 248 rows, and the only large files are 104 GB of raw imaging that needs a GPU to preprocess. The genuinely valuable thing I found is that the paper's published random forest scores R-squared 0.40 on its random split, 0.19 when whole dendrites are held out and -0.14 (worse than the mean) when whole cells are held out, and that its saved model and the Figure 2 network summary are both missing from the deposit.
